answer: The claimant casts a hollow ferrous bell and coats it with a pigment glaze fired in their own kiln; the bell's ring at a named pitch proves the hollow's exact thickness. Two foundry wardens strike the bell and measure its tone against the foundry register within four days, checking the pigment glaze batch against the kiln log. A bell too thick, a tone off pitch, or a bell rung twice voids the season, burns a 240-credit stake, and bars the foundry two seasons. One thousand fake bells mean one thousand hollow castings poured by hand plus one thousand pigment glazes fired one by one.
